newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar eases on trade remark by USTR's Lang.
newsitem.headline: Dollar eases on trade remark by USTR's Lang.

text.p: 0113 GMT --*Dollar eased against yen in mid-morning trade on remarks by USTR official expressing concern about Japan's trade surplus.

*Asked how concerned USTR was by nearly 70 percent rise in Japan's July trade surplus and 35 percent rise in surplus with United States announced earlier on Monday, Deputy USTR Jeffrey Lang told Reuters on Monday: "I haven't seen the trade figures this morning, but we are concerned."
*Dollar earlier rose vs yen on smaller-than-expected trade surplus and Japanese investor buying, dealers said.
*Since dollar's fall on Friday caused losses to traders who held on to dollar longs, traders here wary of building up fresh dollar long positions, dealers said.
*Downside seen supported at around 117.00 yen on buying interest by Japanese investors and short-covering by US funds.
*Traders feel comfortable buying marks vs yen amid growing expectations of higher German interest rates, but Japanese exporter offers seen in place above 65.00 yen.
*Market focusing on Bundesbank's decision on its money market operation on Tuesday and slew of German economic data due out this week.

0002 GMT -- *Dollar edged up against yen after Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus came out at lower end of market expectations. Interbank dealers and Japanese investors seen behind dollar purchases.
*Surplus jumped 69.7 percent in July from a year earlier to 849.08 billion yen, and surplus with United States grew 35.7 percent to 420.55 billion yen.

*"It is not a level at which exporters are placing offers," a dealer at a long-term credit bank said. He said if dollar's topside remains heavy against mark, that may become factor to limit dollar's advance against yen.
